name: Raspberry Wine
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: loaf-sugar per gallon of liquor
ingredients.originalText: 3 pounds of loaf-sugar per gallon of liquor

instructions.text: Put four gallons of ripe raspberries into a stone jar, and mash them with a round stick
Take four gallons of soft water, (measured after it has boiled an hour,) and strain it warm over the raspberries
Stir it well and let it stand twelve hours
Then strain it through a bag, and to every gallon of liquor put three pounds of loaf-sugar
Set it over a clear fire, and boil and skim it till the scum ceases to rise
When it is cold bottle it
Open the bottles every day for a fortnight, closing them again in a few minutes
Then seal the corks, and lay the bottles on their sides in saw-dust, which must not be from pine wood

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put four gallons of ripe raspberries into a stone jar, and mash them with a round stick
2. Take four gallons of soft water, (measured after it has boiled an hour,) and strain it warm over the raspberries
3. Stir it well and let it stand twelve hours
4. Then strain it through a bag, and to every gallon of liquor put three pounds of loaf-sugar
5. Set it over a clear fire, and boil and skim it till the scum ceases to rise
6. When it is cold bottle it
7. Open the bottles every day for a fortnight, closing them again in a few minutes
8. Then seal the corks, and lay the bottles on their sides in saw-dust, which must not be from pine wood
